subject: Re: Governing law & seat — urgent injunctive relief carve?
messages:
From: Sofia Marin <sofia.m@harbortech.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com
Cc: HarborTech Legal <legal@harbortech.com>; Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@harbortech.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Governing law & seat — initial redlines attached

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — HarborTech is keen to move forward but legal has pushed back on a couple of terms in the MSA. Attached is our redline (HT-MSA-Redlines-v3.docx). The key points are: 1) Governing law should be the law of England and Wales (our procurement policy for EU contracts); 2) Seat of dispute: London courts preferred; 3) Carveout for injunctive and urgent equitable relief to be heard in local courts (we asked for immediate injunctive jurisdiction in England or any local HarbourTech office jurisdiction); and 4) explicit waiver of class actions.

We're trying to avoid a long review cycle — can you confirm whether Redwood will accept E&W governing law for this EU purchase, or whether we need to propose a compromise. Also flagging that procurement would like a clean canary: if Redwood refuses E&W, HarborTech may need a limited purchase via our US entity instead.

Files attached: HT-MSA-Redlines-v3.docx (redline), procurement-note.pdf

Appreciate quick turnaround — HarborTech wants to go to signature this week.

Thanks,
Sofia Marin
Head of Procurement — HarborTech
sofia.m@harbortech.com

From: ava_chen@redwood.com <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Marin <sofia.m@harbortech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-01T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Governing law & seat — initial redlines attached

Sofia — thanks for the redline and context. I've looped in Marissa (legal lead) and Jonas (contracts) for review. Quick summary of our stance so we can keep momentum:

- Governing law: Redwood's standard is New York law for commercial MSAs; we can consider E&W for EU-only purchases but need internal sign-off due to precedent and insurance terms.
- Seat/venue: we typically ask for Delaware or New York federal courts as the exclusive forum, with an express carveout for injunctive relief (mutual).
- Injunctive relief: we're open to a mutual, limited carveout allowing either party to seek provisional injunctive relief in local courts, but we generally require that substantive disputes proceed in our chosen seat.

I'll let Marissa and Jonas propose redline language that preserves Redwood's ability to seek a binding resolution in our preferred forum while honoring HarborTech's EU procurement constraints. Attached: Redwood-Proposed-Seat-Compromise.pdf (draft language).

Next step: Marissa, can you review the HT redline and propose a short paragraph we can present back that might be acceptable to HarborTech? Sofia, if you can confirm whether HarborTech requires E&W as a condition of purchase (i.e., can't accept NY law), that will help prioritize the exception path.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-01T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Governing law & seat — initial redlines attached

Ava/Jonas — reviewed HarborTech redline. Key legal notes:

1) Governing law request for England & Wales (E&W) is non-standard for us. It affects indemnity interpretation and our cyber/insurance conflict. Accepting E&W for this deal would require 1) an exceptions request to Risk, and 2) an amendment to our customer standard terms to limit scope (data residency carveouts, audit scope, and limitation on consequential damages need to be adapted).

2) Seat vs. injunctive relief: we can offer a two-part compromise: (a) Governing law: New York (or E&W limited to the EU subsidiary contract) but (b) Forum/seat: exclusive forum in Delaware for substantive disputes, with a narrow, mutual carveout allowing immediate injunctive relief in local courts (including England) to preserve urgent equity. Suggested redline below:

"Notwithstanding the exclusive forum provision, either party may seek provisional injunctive or other equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo, provided that any final adjudication of the dispute shall be brought only in the exclusive forum set forth above."

3) Class action waiver: we accept a mutual waiver; make it reciprocal language.

4) If HarborTech insists on E&W as governing law for the entire agreement, we will need Risk sign-off and (likely) one-time exceptions from Insurance. That will push the timeline by ~5–7 business days.

Action items: Ava — ask HarborTech whether they can accept New York governing law with the mutual injunctive carveout. If they can't, we escalate to Risk for exception. Jonas — please produce a tracked redline that inserts the proposed injunctive sentence and clarifies venue language. Kim — prepare escalation note for Risk if needed.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Sofia Marin <sofia.m@harbortech.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com
Cc: HarborTech Legal <legal@harbortech.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@harbortech.com>
Date: 2028-03-02T09:05:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Governing law & seat — initial redlines attached

Thanks Ava and Marissa — HarborTech legal confirms: we strongly prefer E&W for the EU purchase; moving the whole purchase to our US entity is possible but creates internal billing and VAT headaches we'd rather avoid. We can accept New York only if Redwood agrees to: 1) express carve for English courts to hear provisional injunctive relief; and 2) a 30-day limited consent to service of process in England for enforcement of any provisional orders. Otherwise procurement will delay signature.

We're trying to avoid escalation to Risk since timeline is tight. If you can give us a short, signed MSA with the mutual injunctive carve and a temporary consent for service in England limited to enforcement of provisional orders, that may be acceptable.

Sofia

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Sofia Marin <sofia.m@harbortech.com>, HarborTech Legal <legal@harbortech.com>
Date: 2028-03-02T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Governing law & seat — initial redlines attached

All — quick update: Risk is willing to grant a one-off exception on governing law to New York (with carveouts for EU data residency and audit limits) only if HarborTech accepts the following narrow terms that protect Redwood's ability to obtain final relief in our chosen forum:

- Mutual provisional injunctive carveout (as discussed).
- Limited consent to service in England for 30 days post-signature solely for enforcement of provisional orders (not for substantive litigation).
- Carveout language that any interim orders obtained in England will not bind the final forum's determination on substantive remedies.

I've uploaded a tracked draft with the exact sentence insertions to the shared Drive (see link in metadata). Jonas, please prepare the tracked redline and send to Sofia with a short cover note that this is Redwood's final compromise to keep the deal on the fast path. If HarborTech signs off, Procurement can finalize and Finance will issue PO.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
